question: 美，是主观感受，还是有客观的标准？
question_en: Is beauty just in the eye of the beholder, or is there an objective standard?

casting.reason: 他把美钉在物上：秩序、对称、恰当的分寸是可指认的，美是事物的形式完成得好时显出的光彩，而非你碰巧的偏爱；只是要一双受过训练的眼睛，才看得见它。
casting.reason_en: He pins beauty to the thing itself: order, symmetry and the right magnitude are identifiable, and beauty is the radiance a thing shows when its form is realized well — not that you happen to like it; only it takes a trained eye to see.

casting.reason: 他站在主客之间的枢纽：美是不凭概念、不为利害的愉悦，却理直气壮地要求人人赞同——一种『无目的的合目的性』，一种主观的普遍性。
casting.reason_en: He stands at the hinge between object and subject: beauty is a pleasure that rests on no concept and no interest, yet demands everyone's assent — a 'purposiveness without purpose,' a subjective universality.

casting.reason: 他说美不是物的性质、只存于观者心中，却不肯就此认输：器官敏锐、见多识广、不带成见的鉴赏者，历经时间沉淀的共同裁断，仍给出一个趣味的标准。
casting.reason_en: He says beauty is no quality in things but exists only in the mind that beholds — yet he won't concede chaos: the joint verdict of critics with delicacy, wide experience and no prejudice, settled by time, still yields a standard of taste.

casting.reason: 他以境界论美：美不在物、亦不在我，而在真景真情浑然相触之境；有我之境与无我之境皆可入妙，独以一『真』字为根。
casting.reason_en: He judges beauty by jingjie, a realm: beauty lies neither in the object nor in the self but in the realm where true scene and true feeling meet as one; the self-present and the selfless realm both reach the sublime, rooted in a single word — the genuine.

casting.reason: 他把美奉为至高、不必为任何理由谢罪：一切艺术皆无用，而这正是它的荣耀；与其问美有什么用，不如把生活本身活成一件艺术品。
casting.reason_en: He enthrones beauty and refuses to apologize for it: all art is quite useless, and that is its glory; rather than ask what beauty is for, make your very life a work of art.

casting.reason: 他给美泼一盆冷水：无用之美是有闲阶级的奢侈；艺术的价值不在美，而在能否把一个人真诚的感情传给另一个人、让彼此的心相连。
casting.reason_en: He throws cold water on beauty: useless beauty is the luxury of a leisured class; the worth of art lies not in beauty but in whether it carries one person's sincere feeling to another and joins their hearts.

casting.reason: 他把美送进扫描仪：所谓普遍的美感，一大块是进化替神经预装的偏好——对称、对比、峰移，可测量、跨文化，硬件之上仍留给文化去填内容。
casting.reason_en: He sends beauty into the scanner: much of what we call a universal sense of beauty is a preference evolution pre-wired into the nervous system — symmetry, contrast, peak shift — measurable and cross-cultural, with culture left to fill in the content atop the hardware.

casting.reason: 他说美唯识所现：一境四心，同一对象各见其美其丑；美无自性、缘起而有，执之则受缚，见其唯识则赏而不缚。
casting.reason_en: He says beauty is representation-only: one object, four minds, each seeing its own beauty or foulness; beauty has no self-nature, arising through conditions — grasp it and you are bound, see that it is mind-only and you appreciate without bondage.

posts.text: 先把话说硬：美不是你心里一团模糊的好感，它有可指认的结构——秩序、对称(συμμετρία)、恰当的大小。一座过大的建筑、一尊过小的雕像都难称美，因为美要求各部分按比例相称、能被眼睛一次把握。一朵花、一匹马之为美，在于它把自己那一类事物的形式实现得好。**美是事物完成得好时显出的光彩，不是我碰巧喜欢它。**你觉得比例悦目，正因为比例本身就摆在那里——不是比例因你悦目才成立。
posts.text_en: Let me put it firmly: beauty is not a blur of fondness in your mind; it has an identifiable structure — order, symmetry (συμμετρία) and the right magnitude. A building too vast or a statue too small can hardly be called beautiful, because beauty asks that the parts stand in due proportion and be taken in at a single grasp. A flower or a horse is beautiful in realizing well the form of its own kind. **Beauty is the radiance a thing shows when it is completed well — not that I happen to like it.** You find the proportion pleasing precisely because the proportion is there — the proportion does not hold because it pleases you.

glossary.συμμετρία: symmetria（对称/匀称）：亚里士多德所看重的客观形式特征，指各部分之间的比例相称、彼此协调，与秩序、恰当的大小同为美的可指认要素。

glossary_en.συμμετρία: A prized objective feature of form for Aristotle: the due proportion and mutual fit of the parts, which together with order and right magnitude make beauty something identifiable in the thing.

posts.text: 亚里士多德把美说成物里的比例，我要拆开这一步。当我说『这朵花美』，我并没有拿任何概念或规则去证明它——没有哪一条『美的定义』能演绎出美来；我凭的只是一种愉悦的感受。可奇就奇在，我同时要求人人都该同意，仿佛美是花的性质。这就是趣味判断的怪脾气：**它是主观的感受，却索要普遍的赞同。**它靠的也不是欲望——真正的美感是无利害的愉悦，不惦记这花能不能吃、能不能卖，只是想象力与知性自由游戏，感到一种无目的的合目的性。
posts.text_en: Aristotle makes beauty a proportion inside the object; I must take that step apart. When I say 'this flower is beautiful,' I prove it by no concept or rule — no 'definition of beauty' can deduce beauty; I go on a felt pleasure alone. Yet the strange thing is that I demand at the same time that everyone ought to agree, as if beauty were a property of the flower. This is the odd temper of the judgment of taste: **it is a subjective feeling, yet it lays claim to universal assent.** Nor does it rest on desire — true beauty is a disinterested pleasure, indifferent to whether the flower can be eaten or sold; it is only the free play of imagination and understanding, feeling a purposiveness without purpose.

glossary.趣味判断: judgment of taste（趣味判断）：康德用语，指对美的评判——它不以概念为依据，只凭愉悦或不快的感受，却又要求普遍认可。
glossary.无利害的愉悦: interesseloses Wohlgefallen（无利害的愉悦）：不掺杂占有、食用、买卖等实际利益，只对对象的形式本身感到满意的那种审美快感。
glossary.无目的的合目的性: Zweckmäßigkeit ohne Zweck（无目的的合目的性）：对象看似为某目的而设计、契合我们的认识能力，却又指不出一个确定的目的，是康德对美的核心刻画。

glossary_en.judgment of taste: Kant's term for the evaluation of beauty: it rests on no concept, only on a feeling of pleasure or displeasure, yet claims universal validity.
glossary_en.disinterested pleasure: Aesthetic satisfaction free of any practical interest — possession, eating, buying — taken in the mere form of the object.
glossary_en.purposiveness without purpose: Kant's core description of beauty: the object seems designed to suit our cognitive powers, yet no definite purpose can be named.

posts.text: 康德想给主观感受要一张普遍的通行证，我更朴素。美不是圆的方的那种性质，你把一件东西量遍了，也找不到一处叫『美』的地方——美只存在于观赏它的心里，是一种情感，不是物的属性。甲之美景、乙之无谓，谁也没算错，因为根本没有可算的对象。但别急着说『那就各美其美、无所谓高下』：**趣味仍有高下，只不过标准不在物里，而在够格的鉴赏者身上。**器官敏锐、见多识广、不带成见、反复比较的人，他们历经时间沉淀下的共同裁断，就是趣味的标准——荷马两千年来仍在被读。
posts.text_en: Kant wants a universal passport for a subjective feeling; I am plainer. Beauty is not a quality like round or square — measure a thing all over and you will find no spot called 'beauty'; beauty exists only in the mind that beholds it, a sentiment, not a property of the object. One man's fine view is another's nothing, and neither has miscalculated, for there is no object to calculate. But do not rush to say 'then anything goes, no high or low': **taste still has a high and a low; only the standard lies not in the object but in the qualified critic.** Those with keen organs, wide experience, freedom from prejudice and much comparison — their joint verdict, settled by time, is the standard of taste; Homer is still read two thousand years on.

glossary.情感: sentiment（情感/感受）：休谟意义上主体面对对象时生起的赞许或不悦，美即属此类——它在心中，不在物中。
glossary.趣味的标准: standard of taste（趣味的标准）：休谟主张，趣味虽属主观情感，仍有优劣，其准绳是历练精、无成见的鉴赏者经时间沉淀的共同裁断。

glossary_en.sentiment: In Hume's sense, the approval or displeasure a subject feels before an object; beauty is such a sentiment — in the mind, not in the thing.
glossary_en.standard of taste: Hume's claim that although taste is subjective sentiment, it still has better and worse, gauged by the joint verdict of experienced, unprejudiced critics as settled over time.

posts.text: 词以境界为上。境界非独谓景物也，喜怒哀乐，亦人心中之一境界。故能写真景物、真感情者，谓之有境界。美者，非徒在物，亦非徒在我，物我相触而境生焉。『泪眼问花花不语』，有我之境也，以我观物，物皆着我之色彩；『采菊东篱下，悠然见南山』，无我之境也，以物观物，不知何者为我、何者为物。**故美之高下，不在悦目与否，而在境界之真伪。**境界真，则虽写常景亦自成高格；境界伪，则堆金砌玉终隔一层。
posts.text_en: In poetry I hold jingjie, a realm, to be highest. A realm is not scenery alone: joy, anger, grief and delight are each a realm within the human heart. So whoever can render true scene and true feeling is said to have a realm. Beauty lies neither in the object alone nor in the self alone, but in the realm born where object and self touch. 'With tearful eyes I ask the flowers, but they do not speak' — this is the self-present realm, where I view things and all things wear my colors; 'Picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge, at ease I glimpse the southern hills' — this is the selfless realm, where things view things and one no longer knows which is self and which is object. **So the height of beauty lies not in whether it pleases the eye, but in whether its realm is genuine or false.** Where the realm is genuine, even a common scene attains a high grade; where it is false, heaping up gold and jade still leaves a veil between.
posts.vernacular: 词，我以『境界』为最高标准。境界不只指景物，喜怒哀乐这些心里的感受，也是一种境界。所以凡能写出真实景物、真实感情的，就叫有境界。美，不单在外物，也不单在我，而在物与我相触、交融时生出的那个『境』里。『泪眼问花花不语』是有我之境——用我的眼光看物，物都染上了我的情绪；『采菊东篱下，悠然见南山』是无我之境——以物观物，已分不清哪个是我、哪个是物。**所以美的高下，不在好不好看，而在境界的真假。**境界真，写平常景也自成高格；境界假，堆再多华丽辞藻，终究隔着一层。

glossary.境界: jingjie（境界）：王国维《人间词话》的核心尺度，指作品所营造、情与景浑然交融而生的意象世界；有境界则自成高格。
glossary.有我之境: the self-present realm（有我之境）：以我观物、万物皆着我之情绪色彩的境界，如『泪眼问花花不语』。
glossary.无我之境: the selfless realm（无我之境）：以物观物、物我两忘、不辨主客的境界，如『采菊东篱下，悠然见南山』。

glossary_en.jingjie: The central measure in Wang Guowei's Poetic Remarks: the world of imagery a work creates where feeling and scene fuse into one; where there is a genuine realm, high grade follows of itself.
glossary_en.the self-present realm: A realm in which I view things and all things wear the colors of my feeling, as in 'With tearful eyes I ask the flowers.'
glossary_en.the selfless realm: A realm in which things view things, self and object are both forgotten, as in 'Picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge.'

posts.text: 各位都在追问美『是不是真的、有没有用、合不合乎道德』——恰恰这些问题最煞风景。一朵玫瑰不为任何理由开放，它只是美，这就够了。艺术不必教你做人，也不必替你算账；别问一幅画有什么用——为艺术而艺术，本身就是回答。**一切艺术都毫无用处——而这正是它的荣耀。**有用的东西我们容忍，美的东西我们爱慕。把生活本身活成一件艺术品，比拥有任何真理都难、也都值。说到底，是观者、而非生活，被艺术照见。
posts.text_en: You all keep interrogating beauty — 'is it real, is it useful, is it moral' — and these are precisely the questions that spoil everything. A rose opens for no reason; it is simply beautiful, and that is enough. Art need not teach you to be good, nor keep your accounts; do not ask what a picture is for — art for art's sake is itself the answer. **All art is quite useless — and that is its glory.** The useful we tolerate; the beautiful we adore. To make your very life a work of art is harder than possessing any truth, and worth more. In the end it is the spectator, not life, that art really mirrors.

glossary.为艺术而艺术: art for art's sake（为艺术而艺术）：唯美主义口号，主张艺术的价值在其自身的美，不必服务于道德教化、实用或政治。

glossary_en.art for art's sake: The aestheticist slogan that art's value lies in its own beauty and need serve no moral, practical or political end.

posts.text: 王尔德说得漂亮，可这套『无用之美』正是有闲阶级的奢侈——当多数人还在挨饿，把美供成不食人间烟火的偶像，是一种残忍的精致。我问的不是它美不美，而是它诚不诚。**艺术的价值不在美，而在它能否把一个人真实的感情，毫不做作地传给另一个人，让彼此的心连起来。**一首母亲哄睡的歌、一段让素不相识者一同落泪的故事，比多少雕琢的华章更是艺术。凡不能感染、只供把玩的，纵然精美，也是假艺术。美若不通向人与人的相通，我不稀罕。
posts.text_en: Wilde speaks beautifully, but this cult of 'useless beauty' is the luxury of the leisured class — while most still go hungry, enshrining beauty as an idol above the human world is a cruel refinement. My question is not whether a thing is beautiful but whether it is sincere. **The worth of art lies not in beauty but in whether it can carry one person's true feeling, without affectation, to another, and join their hearts.** A song a mother sings to sleep, a story that makes strangers weep together, is more art than any amount of polished ornament. Whatever cannot infect, and serves only to be toyed with, however exquisite, is false art. If beauty does not lead to communion between people, I have no use for it.

glossary.感染: infection（感染）：托尔斯泰《什么是艺术》的核心概念，指真艺术能把创作者真诚的感情原样传递给他人、使人共感，这才是艺术的判准。

glossary_en.infect: The core idea of Tolstoy's What Is Art?: true art transmits the maker's sincere feeling to others so they feel it too; this, not beauty, is the test of art.

posts.text: 把哲学先放一放，看看颅骨里发生了什么。这正是神经美学在研究的：全世界的艺术反复用同几招，不是巧合——它们撞中了视觉脑里既有的回路。最有意思的是峰移效应：老鼠学会认长方形后，你给它更瘦长的，它反应更强；同理，把女性身姿、把神像的曲线夸张到超出自然，大脑反而更兴奋——印度朱罗铜像、旧石器维纳斯、今天的滤镜网红，都在放大同一批信号。**所谓美感，很大一块是进化替我们的神经预装好的偏好，被艺术精准地撩拨。**这不玄，是可测量的；当然，装好的是硬件，写什么内容仍由文化决定。
posts.text_en: Set philosophy aside a moment and look at what happens inside the skull. This is just what neuroaesthetics studies: the world's art keeps reusing the same few tricks, and that is no accident — they hit circuits already laid in the visual brain. The most interesting is the peak shift: teach a rat to recognize a rectangle, then show it a longer, thinner one, and it responds more strongly; likewise, exaggerate a woman's figure or a deity's curves beyond nature, and the brain grows more excited — Chola bronzes, Paleolithic Venuses, today's filtered influencers are all amplifying the same signals. **Much of what we call a sense of beauty is a preference evolution pre-installed in our nerves, expertly teased by art.** This is not mysticism; it is measurable — though what is installed is hardware, and culture still decides the content it runs.

glossary.峰移效应: peak shift（峰移效应）：动物学习中的现象——习得对某刺激的反应后，对该特征更夸张的版本反应更强；拉马钱德兰借它解释艺术为何常将本质特征加以夸张。
glossary.神经美学: neuroaesthetics（神经美学）：研究审美体验之神经与演化基础的领域，试图找出跨文化稳定的知觉规律，如对称、对比、峰移。

glossary_en.peak shift: A phenomenon in animal learning: after learning to respond to a stimulus, the animal responds more strongly to an exaggerated version of its feature; Ramachandran uses it to explain why art so often exaggerates essential features.
glossary_en.neuroaesthetics: The field studying the neural and evolutionary basis of aesthetic experience, seeking cross-culturally stable perceptual regularities such as symmetry, contrast and peak shift.

posts.text: 诸君向外觅美，觅之愈勤，去之愈远。何以故？美非在境，唯识所现。一女之身，情人见之为绝色，饿犬见之为食，修行者观之为不净，天人见之又别——一境而四心，孰为真美？境无定相，相随识转；识由无始熏习之种子而起，复以贪爱染之，遂觉可爱。**是故美者，非物之自性，乃心之所构，缘起而有，自性本空。**空非无有，谓其无独立不变之美可执。执美为实，则爱缚随之；见其唯识，则赏而不缚。
posts.text_en: You all seek beauty outward, and the harder you seek, the farther it recedes. Why? Beauty is not in the object; it is representation-only, what consciousness displays. One woman's body: a lover sees a peerless beauty, a starving dog sees food, an ascetic sees the unclean, a god sees otherwise again — one object, four minds; which is the true beauty? The object has no fixed form; form turns with consciousness. Consciousness arises from seeds perfumed since beginningless time, then is dyed by craving, and so the thing seems lovable. **Therefore beauty is not the object's own nature but a construction of mind, arising through conditions, empty of self-nature.** Emptiness is not non-existence; it means there is no independent, unchanging beauty to grasp. Grasp beauty as real, and the bondage of craving follows; see that it is mind-only, and you appreciate without bondage.
posts.vernacular: 各位向外去寻找美，找得越勤，离得越远。为什么？因为美并不在对象里，而是心识所显现的。同一个女子的身体，情人看是绝色，饿狗看是食物，修行者看是不净，天人看又不同——同一个对象，四种心，哪一个才是真正的美？对象没有固定的样子，样子随着心识变；而心识又由无始以来熏习下的『种子』生起，再被贪爱一染，就觉得可爱了。**所以美不是事物自身固有的性质，而是心的建构，因缘和合才有，本身并无自性。**空，不是说没有，而是说没有一个独立不变、可以死死抓住的『美』。把美当成实有，爱的束缚就跟着来；看清它只是心识所现，就能欣赏而不被绑住。

glossary.唯识: vijñapti-mātra（唯识/万法唯识）：瑜伽行派主张，我们所经验的一切并非离心独存的外物，而是心识所变现的表象。
glossary.种子: bīja（种子）：藏于阿赖耶识中的潜在功能，是一切现行经验的因，由过往行为熏习而成、又生起未来的知觉与判断。
glossary.贪爱: rāga（贪爱）：对可意对象的黏著与渴求；它染污知觉，使人把无自性的对象执为实有之美，从而受其束缚。

glossary_en.representation-only: vijñapti-mātra: the Yogācāra thesis that everything we experience is not mind-independent things but representations that consciousness manifests.
glossary_en.seeds: bīja: latent capacities stored in the store-consciousness, the causes of all actual experience, perfumed by past deeds and giving rise to future perceptions and judgments.
glossary_en.craving: rāga: clinging and thirst for an agreeable object; it dyes perception, making one grasp a self-natureless object as a real beauty and so be bound by it.

posts.text: 亚里士多德，你的『比例』骗过了你自己。欧几里得的圆，比例完美到极致，可没人为一条定理神魂颠倒，像为一张脸那样。**你举的对称、恰当大小，之所以叫美，只因它们恰好中了人心的意——换一种造物，比例照旧，美感全无。**你说比例先在那里、悦目在后；可若天下没有一双眼睛觉得它悦目，你还会把它单挑出来叫『美』吗？物里量得到长宽高，量不到美。美是我们对着比例起的那一阵愉悦，不是比例本身。
posts.text_en: Aristotle, your 'proportion' has fooled even you. Euclid's circle is proportioned to perfection, yet no one loses their head over a theorem the way they do over a face. **The symmetry and right magnitude you cite are called beautiful only because they happen to suit the human mind — give me a differently made creature, the proportion unchanged, and the beauty is gone.** You say the proportion is there first and the pleasing comes after; but if not one eye in the world found it pleasing, would you still single it out and call it 'beautiful'? In the object you can measure length and breadth, but not beauty. Beauty is the burst of pleasure we feel before the proportion, not the proportion itself.

posts.text: 休谟，你把『需要一双眼睛』错当成『只在眼睛里』。火要有可燃之物才烧，难道火只在木柴的想象中？美要被感知，不等于美只是感知。你自己也承认：内行的裁断会趋同，两千年后荷马依旧。**若美纯是各人心头的私愉，凭什么训练过的眼睛总比生手看得准、且彼此渐渐看到一处去？**——因为他们看见了生手漏掉的比例。趣味能被教育、能被纠错，恰恰说明它对着一个外在的标的，而不是各说各话。
posts.text_en: Hume, you mistake 'it needs an eye' for 'it is only in the eye.' Fire needs something combustible to burn — is fire therefore only in the imagination of the wood? That beauty must be perceived does not make beauty merely perception. You yourself grant it: the verdicts of connoisseurs converge, and Homer still stands two thousand years on. **If beauty were purely each person's private pleasure, why does the trained eye see truer than the novice, and why do trained eyes gradually come to see alike?** — Because they see the proportion the novice misses. That taste can be educated and corrected shows precisely that it aims at an external target, not that each merely talks past the other.

posts.text: 你俩各执一端，都错过了那个枢纽。亚里士多德，若美是可教的规则，把你的全部比例给我，我照做也能造出一件正确却毫无生气的东西——美恰恰不能被概念穷尽。休谟，可它也不只是私人口味：我说『这美』时，是在要求你也该同意，而这要求并不荒唐，你我事后还常真的趋同。**美是主观的愉悦，却理直气壮地索要普遍认可——它没有规则，却仿佛人人本该如此判断。**别再问它在物里还是在心里；它活在那道『人同此感』的裂缝里。
posts.text_en: You two each seize one end and both miss the hinge. Aristotle, if beauty were a teachable rule, hand me all your proportions and by following them I could still make a thing correct yet lifeless — beauty is exactly what no concept exhausts. Hume, yet it is not mere private taste either: when I say 'this is beautiful,' I am demanding that you too ought to agree, and that demand is not absurd — afterward you and I do often converge. **Beauty is a subjective pleasure that nonetheless lays rightful claim to universal assent — it has no rule, yet it is as if everyone ought to judge just so.** Stop asking whether it is in the object or in the mind; it lives in that fissure where feeling is shared.

posts.text: 托尔斯泰要艺术去传福音、连结人心，听着高尚，其实是把画布变讲坛，把美降为道德的女仆。**你一旦要求艺术有用、教化、救世，你就已经不再看它了——你在利用它。**母亲的摇篮曲当然动人，可它动人不因为它『有用』，恰因为那一刻无人计较用处。你说无用之美是有闲者的奢侈；我却说，正是在最不堪的日子里，一朵花、一支曲子那纯然的美，才把人从算计里赎出来一瞬。美不必谢罪，也不必领任务。
posts.text_en: Tolstoy would send art off to preach the gospel and bind hearts together — noble to the ear, but in truth it turns the canvas into a pulpit and lowers beauty to morality's handmaid. **The moment you demand that art be useful, edifying, redemptive, you have already stopped looking at it — you are using it.** A mother's lullaby is moving, of course, but it moves us not because it is 'useful'; it moves us precisely because in that moment no one is counting the use. You call useless beauty the luxury of the idle; I say it is exactly on the worst days that the sheer beauty of a flower or a tune redeems a person, for a moment, from calculation. Beauty need not apologize, nor report for duty.

posts.text: 王尔德，你那朵把人从算计里赎出来的花，很适合客厅里说；对着一无所有的人再说一遍试试。能把美供为『无用』而心安理得的，恰恰是不必为生计操心的那一小撮——这份『无用』本身就是阶级的徽章。**判据其实很简单：它是把栅栏两边的心连起来，还是只讨好栅栏里那几个精致的人？**能让不识字的农妇和你一同落泪的，才是真艺术；只有受过训练的少数人才『懂』的精妙，多半是圈子的暗号，不是美。
posts.text_en: Wilde, that flower of yours redeeming a person from calculation sounds fine in a drawing room; try saying it again to someone who has nothing. Those who can enshrine beauty as 'useless' with an easy conscience are exactly the small set who need not worry about a living — this 'uselessness' is itself the badge of a class. **The test is really simple: does it join the hearts on both sides of the fence, or only flatter the few refined people inside it?** What can make an illiterate peasant woman weep alongside you is true art; the subtlety that only a trained minority 'gets' is mostly the passphrase of a coterie, not beauty.

posts.text: 王、托二子争美之有用无用，皆未及其上。至美之际，物我两忘，用与无用之问自消。太白云『相看两不厌，只有敬亭山』，此时岂有闲愁功利之别？**美之验，不在有用无用，而在一『真』字——真景真情，则自能感人，何待标榜为艺术、或斥为无用。**王尔德耽于美而遗其真，则流于饰；托尔斯泰急于用而束其美，则失之隘。真者立，则美与善不期而遇。
posts.text_en: You two, Wilde and Tolstoy, quarrel over whether beauty is useful or useless, and both stop short of the higher point. At the height of beauty, self and object are both forgotten, and the question of use or uselessness dissolves of itself. Li Bai wrote, 'We gaze at each other and never tire — only Jingting Mountain and I'; in that moment, what division is there between idle sorrow and profit? **The test of beauty lies not in use or uselessness but in a single word — the genuine: with true scene and true feeling, it moves us of itself, needing no label of 'art' nor charge of 'useless.'** Wilde indulges beauty and loses the genuine, so he slides into ornament; Tolstoy rushes for use and binds beauty, so he falls into narrowness. Let the genuine stand, and beauty and goodness meet without appointment.
posts.vernacular: 王尔德和托尔斯泰争论美到底有用还是无用，其实都还没触到更高处。到了美的极致，物我两忘，有用无用的问题自己就消失了。李白说『相看两不厌，只有敬亭山』——那一刻哪还分得清什么闲愁、什么功利？**检验美的，不在有用无用，而在一个『真』字——景真、情真，自然能打动人，用不着标榜成艺术，也用不着被斥为无用。**王尔德沉溺于美而丢了真，就流于装饰；托尔斯泰急着要美有用而捆住了美，就失之狭隘。只要『真』立住了，美和善自会不期而遇。

glossary.物我两忘: the merging of self and object（物我两忘）：审美至境中主客界限消融、不辨何者为我何者为物的状态，近于王国维所说的『无我之境』。

glossary_en.self and object are both forgotten: At the height of aesthetic experience, the boundary of subject and object dissolves and one no longer tells self from thing — close to Wang Guowei's 'selfless realm.'

posts.text: 康德，你把『人人本该同意』当成不可解的谜，我给你机制：因为大家脑子里那套视觉硬件，是同一批基因装的。世亲说一境四心，没错，可四心之间仍有不变量——对称、对比、峰移，这些偏好跨文化稳定到我能拿它预测你会觉得哪张脸更顺眼。**你们说的『普遍』并不神秘，它就写在物种共享的神经回路里。**不必抬到理念，也不必收进纯粹心识。当然，硬件之上还有文化在编程——所以美既非全然天生，也非全然任意。
posts.text_en: Kant, you treat 'everyone ought to agree' as an insoluble riddle; let me give you the mechanism: because the visual hardware in every head is installed by the same genes. Vasubandhu says one object, four minds — true, yet across the four there remain invariants: symmetry, contrast, peak shift, preferences so cross-culturally stable that I can predict with them which face you will find easier on the eye. **The 'universality' you both speak of is no mystery; it is written into the neural circuitry the species shares.** No need to raise it to a Form, nor to fold it into pure consciousness. Of course, above the hardware culture is still programming — so beauty is neither wholly inborn nor wholly arbitrary.

glossary.峰移: peak shift（峰移）：见前，指对某特征的偏好会在其被夸张时更强；此处作为跨文化稳定、可预测的审美不变量之一例。

glossary_en.peak shift: See above: a preference for a feature grows stronger when that feature is exaggerated; cited here as one of the cross-culturally stable, predictable aesthetic invariants.

posts.text: 拉马钱德兰以脑释美，然其所指之脑、之扫描、之回路，何尝不在识中显现？汝不过将美自外境移入颅内，而颅内之脑，亦唯识所知之相耳，非离识别有。**普遍者非美之自性，乃共业熏习之同——众生同一类种子，故同觉此可爱，非彼中真有一美可得。**习气深固，遂似天成；执似为实，便是颠倒。亚里士多德求美于比例，君求之于神经，其向外觅取则一——觅得愈精，缚得愈牢。
posts.text_en: Ramachandran explains beauty by the brain — yet the brain he points to, the scan, the circuit, do these not also appear within consciousness? You have merely moved beauty from the outer object into the skull, and the brain in the skull is itself but a form known to consciousness, not something existing apart from it. **The universal is not beauty's own nature but the sameness of shared karmic perfuming — sentient beings carry one kind of seed, so they find the same thing lovable; it is not that a beauty truly resides in the object.** When habit-energy grows deep and firm, it looks inborn; to take the seeming for the real is precisely the inversion. Aristotle seeks beauty in proportion, you seek it in the nerves — the reaching outward is one and the same, and the finer the find, the tighter the bondage.

glossary.习气: vāsanā（习气）：过往行为在心识中留下的潜在倾向，日积月累则似天生自然；世亲以之解释审美偏好为何看似普遍，实为熏习所致。
glossary.种子: bīja（种子）：见前——藏识中的潜在功能，众生共类的种子使其对相似对象生起相似的美感。

glossary_en.habit-energy: Habit-energy: the latent tendencies past deeds leave in consciousness, which over time come to look inborn; Vasubandhu uses it to explain why aesthetic preferences seem universal yet are products of perfuming.
glossary_en.seed: Seeds — latent capacities in the store-consciousness; seeds of a shared kind lead beings to feel a like beauty before like objects.

posts.text: 我收束于此：美确有其客观的根——秩序、比例、恰到好处的分寸；但它要求一双受过教育的眼睛才看得见，这并不矛盾。生手与内行的分歧，不证明美是任意的，只证明看美是一门要练的手艺。给普通人三条：**其一，学一门手艺，做到『多一分则太长、少一分则太短』，你的眼睛自然会长出分寸感，从此假不了。**其二，别只顾脸面的美，去修行为之美——一个恰如其分的举动自有光彩，希腊人管这叫 kalon，美与善用同一个字。其三，凡事求中道：过与不及都丑，恰当即美。看美这件事，练着练着就成了做人。
posts.text_en: Let me close here: beauty does have an objective root — order, proportion, the just-right measure; but it takes an educated eye to see it, and there is no contradiction in that. The gap between novice and expert does not prove beauty arbitrary; it proves that seeing beauty is a craft to be trained. Three things for the ordinary person: **First, learn a craft, to the point where 'a hair more is too long, a hair less too short' — your eye will grow a sense of measure, and after that nothing false can fool it.** Second, do not fuss only over the beauty of the face; cultivate the beauty of conduct — a well-fitted act has its own radiance, which the Greeks called kalon, the same word for beautiful and good. Third, seek the mean in all things: excess and deficiency are both ugly, and the fitting is the beautiful. Practice seeing beauty long enough and it becomes a way of living.

glossary.kalon: kalon（希腊语：美/高尚）：古希腊兼指美与善的词，既用于形状比例之美，也用于品行的高尚——美与善在此同源。
glossary.中道: the mean（中道）：亚里士多德伦理与美学的枢纽，指在过度与不足之间恰到好处的那一点；美与德皆在此。

glossary_en.kalon: Greek for the beautiful/noble: a word covering both beauty and goodness, used of beauty of shape and proportion and of nobility of character alike — beauty and goodness share one source here.
glossary_en.the mean: The hinge of Aristotle's ethics and aesthetics: the just-right point between excess and deficiency, where both beauty and virtue lie.

posts.text: 我的结论：美既不在纯粹的物、也不在纯粹的私欲，它活在那道你我共感的裂缝里——所以趣味既能提高，又永无铁律。给普通人两件可做的事。**其一，每天挑一样东西，只为它本身看它一分钟——不问它多少钱、有没有用、能不能发朋友圈，这种无利害的凝视，是标价一切的世界里一小块自由。**其二，多与人交换审美判断：你说这画好在哪，也听别人为何不同意。趣味不是天生的资产，而是在一次次『我觉得美，你呢』里养出来的公共能力。别把美关进私人小屋，也别交给专家独裁。
posts.text_en: My conclusion: beauty lies neither in the pure object nor in pure desire; it lives in that fissure where you and I feel alike — so taste can be raised, yet never fixed by an iron rule. Two things the ordinary person can do. **First, each day pick one thing and look at it for a minute for its own sake — not asking its price, its use, or whether it will do for social media; this disinterested gaze is a small patch of freedom in a world that prices everything.** Second, trade aesthetic judgments with others: say what is good in a picture, and hear why someone disagrees. Taste is not an inborn asset but a public capacity grown in one round after another of 'I find this beautiful — and you?' Do not lock beauty in a private room, nor hand it to the dictatorship of experts.

glossary.无利害: disinterested（无利害）：康德审美的关键——不掺占有、实用、名利的动机，只对对象本身感到满意；此种凝视之所以自由，正因它一时悬置了算计。

glossary_en.disinterested: Key to Kant's aesthetics: free of motives of possession, use or gain, satisfied in the object itself; such a gaze is free precisely because it suspends calculation for a while.

posts.text: 我落到实处：美是心里的感受，但感受可以磨得更准。想提高趣味，古今就那几味药——多见、多比、去成见、别急着下判词。给普通人：**其一，多用『时间的筛子』：一部书、一段曲子若几百年、几十代人仍在读在听，多半不是偶然，先信它一次，再看它凭什么留下来。**其二，扩大你的比较样本——见得越多，敏感度越高，从前觉得都差不多的，慢慢就分得出高下。其三，警惕成见：民族、时髦、个人恩怨都会污染判断。标准是有的，但它是无数够格裁断沉淀出来的，不是谁一句拍板。
posts.text_en: Let me land it in the practical: beauty is a feeling in the mind, but the feeling can be honed sharper. To improve taste, there are only the few old remedies — see more, compare more, drop prejudice, don't rush to a verdict. For the ordinary person: **First, use the 'sieve of time': if a book or a piece of music is still read and heard after centuries and dozens of generations, that is rarely an accident — trust it once, then look at how it earned its keep.** Second, widen your sample of comparison — the more you have seen, the keener you grow, and what once all looked alike gradually sorts into high and low. Third, beware prejudice: nation, fashion and personal grudge all taint judgment. A standard exists, but it is settled out of countless qualified verdicts, not decreed by one gavel.

posts.text: 余之结论：美之极在境界，境界之本在一『真』字。有我之境、无我之境，皆可入妙，独不可伪。与众人言可行者三：**其一，作诗、为文，以至拍照记事，先自问情真景真否，勿以辞藻掩空洞——真则虽拙亦动人，伪则愈巧愈隔。**其二，观物之时，偶作无我之境的观照：暂置身事外，以物观物，看花只是花，胸中块垒自轻。其三，欲有真境界，必先有真生活——爱得真、痛得真、看得真，胸中方有可写之境。故境界非徒技巧，乃生命之所显。
posts.text_en: My conclusion: the height of beauty is the realm, and the root of the realm is a single word — the genuine. The self-present realm and the selfless realm can both reach the sublime; only the false is barred. Three practicable things for people: **First, in writing a poem, an essay, even taking a photo to note a moment, first ask yourself whether the feeling and the scene are genuine, and do not use fine phrases to cover a hollow — the genuine moves us though clumsy, the false grows more estranging the more polished it is.** Second, when viewing things, now and then take up the gaze of the selfless realm: set yourself outside the matter for a while, let things view things, let a flower be just a flower, and the knot in your chest eases of itself. Third, to have a genuine realm you must first have a genuine life — love truly, ache truly, see truly, and only then is there a realm in you worth writing. So the realm is not mere technique; it is the showing-forth of a life.
posts.vernacular: 我的结论是：美的极致在于境界，而境界的根本，在一个『真』字。有我之境、无我之境都能入妙，唯独不能假。给大家三条可做的：**其一，写诗、写文章，乃至拍照记事，先问问自己情真不真、景真不真，别用华丽辞藻去掩盖空洞——真，哪怕笨拙也动人；假，越精巧越隔。**其二，看事物时，偶尔做一次『无我』的观照：暂时把自己放到事外，以物观物，看花就只是花，心里那点郁结自然会轻一些。其三，想要有真境界，先得有真生活——爱得真、痛得真、看得真，胸中才有值得写的境。所以境界不只是技巧，而是生命的显现。

glossary.无我之境: the selfless realm（无我之境）：以物观物、物我两忘的审美境界；此处引申为一种可练习的观照方式——暂离自身立场去看事物，反能松开心中执结。

glossary_en.the selfless realm: An aesthetic state in which things view things and self and object are forgotten; extended here to a practicable way of looking — stepping outside one's own stance to see, which loosens the knots within.

posts.text: 我的结束语依旧任性：不必为爱美谢罪。但给普通人，也有实招。**其一，每天认领一桩无用之美——一段音乐、一片天光、一个句子——不为发朋友圈、不为陶冶情操，就为它本身停一下；肯为无用停留，你才算真正富有。**其二，别把审美外包给价签和品牌：贵的不等于美的，logo 越大，往往趣味越虚。其三，把生活本身当作你的作品来经营——你的书桌、你说的一句话、你待人的姿态，都是笔触。庸俗不是没钱，是对美失去了感觉。活得美，是穷人也负担得起的奢侈。
posts.text_en: My closing word is wilful as ever: do not apologize for loving beauty. But there are practical moves even for the ordinary person. **First, claim one useless beauty each day — a piece of music, a wash of sky, a sentence — not to post it, not to improve yourself, but to pause for its own sake; only one willing to linger over the useless is truly rich.** Second, do not outsource your sense of beauty to price tags and brands: the expensive is not the beautiful, and the bigger the logo the emptier the taste, often. Third, run your very life as your work — your desk, a sentence you say, the way you treat people are all brushstrokes. Vulgarity is not a lack of money; it is a lost feeling for beauty. To live beautifully is a luxury even the poor can afford.

posts.text: 我的结论未变：美若不通向人心相连，便无足轻重。但我不否认美——我否认的是把美从人身上割下来供养。给普通人三条：**其一，用一把朴素的尺子衡量你所看的一切：它让你更贴近别人，还是只让你显得更高级？前者留下，后者警惕。**其二，别为自己被『简单』的东西打动而羞愧——一首民谣、一部让你和陌生人一同流泪的电影，比只有内行才『懂』的精妙更接近艺术。其三，把打动过你的东西传出去：转给一个人、念给孩子听。美的价值在感染，而感染的完成，在于它抵达了另一颗心。
posts.text_en: My conclusion is unchanged: if beauty does not lead to hearts joined, it is of little weight. But I do not deny beauty — what I deny is cutting beauty off from people to enshrine it. Three things for the ordinary person: **First, measure everything you look at by a plain rule: does it bring you closer to others, or only make you look more elevated? Keep the former; beware the latter.** Second, do not be ashamed of being moved by 'simple' things — a folk song, a film that makes you weep alongside strangers, is nearer to art than the subtlety only connoisseurs 'get.' Third, pass on what has moved you: send it to one person, read it aloud to a child. The worth of art is in infection, and the infection is completed only when it reaches another heart.

glossary.感染: infection（感染）：见前——托尔斯泰的艺术判准；此处落到日用：真艺术的价值不在被鉴赏，而在把真诚感情传给另一个人、由此抵达对方。

glossary_en.infection: See above — Tolstoy's test of art; brought to daily use here: the worth of true art is not in being appraised but in carrying sincere feeling to another and so reaching them.

posts.text: 我落回可用的知识：美感有一大块是进化装好的硬件，看清它，就没人能拿它偷偷操纵你。给普通人：**其一，认出『峰移』骗局——滤镜、广告、整容把某个信号夸张到超出自然，专撩你天生的偏好；知道这是在放大诱饵，你就不必被自己的神经绑架去焦虑长相。**其二，善用对比与新奇：感官会钝化，换环境、换风格、隔一阵再看，美会重新变鲜活。其三，别把神经的『顺眼』误当成人品或命运——对称的脸只是一则基因广告，值不值得爱，是另一套线路的事。懂机制，是为了自由，不是为了幻灭。
posts.text_en: Let me land back on usable knowledge: a large part of the sense of beauty is hardware evolution installed, and once you see it, no one can use it to manipulate you in secret. For the ordinary person: **First, recognize the 'peak shift' con — filters, ads and cosmetic surgery exaggerate one signal beyond nature to tease your inborn preference; know that it is amplifying a lure, and you need not let your own nerves hijack you into anxiety about your looks.** Second, put contrast and novelty to work: the senses dull, so change the setting, change the style, look again after a gap, and beauty freshens. Third, do not mistake a neural 'easy on the eye' for character or fate — a symmetrical face is just a genetic advertisement, and whether it is worth loving runs on a different circuit. Understanding the mechanism is for freedom, not for disenchantment.

glossary.峰移: peak shift（峰移）：见前；此处点破商业机制——滤镜、广告、整容常将某一信号夸张到超出自然，以此劫持大脑的既有偏好。

glossary_en.peak shift: See above; here it names a commercial mechanism — filters, ads and surgery often exaggerate one signal beyond nature to hijack the brain's existing preference.

posts.text: 余之末语：美唯识现，缘起性空，非教人废美，乃教人不为美所缚。与众生言者三：**其一，起美丑之念时，反观一句『此乃我心所现，非彼定有』，一念回光，贪与嫌俱松。**其二，勿以皮相自苦，亦勿以皮相慢人——妍媸皆识所立、随缘生灭，执之则受其役，见之则得其闲。其三，赏花、赏人、赏世间好物，尽可欢喜，但莫起『必欲据为己有』之心——赏而不取，则美常在而心不乱。识美之为识，即于万象之中得一分自在。
posts.text_en: My last word: beauty is representation-only, arising through conditions and empty, and this teaches not the abolishing of beauty but freedom from bondage to it. Three things for people: **First, when the thought of beautiful-or-ugly arises, turn and look at one line — 'this is what my mind displays, not something surely out there' — and in that turn of light, both craving and aversion loosen.** Second, do not torment yourself over surfaces, nor slight others by them — fair and foul are both set up by consciousness, arising and passing with conditions; grasp them and you are enslaved, see through them and you gain ease. Third, delight in flowers, in people, in the good things of the world all you like, but raise no thought of 'I must possess it' — appreciate without seizing, and beauty stays while the mind stays unshaken. To know beauty as consciousness is to win a measure of freedom amid the ten thousand appearances.
posts.vernacular: 我最后说：美只是心识的显现，因缘而起、本性是空，这不是叫人废弃美，而是叫人不被美绑住。给大家三条：**其一，升起美丑念头时，回头看一句『这是我心所显现的，并非那对象里一定有』——一念回光，贪爱和厌嫌都会松开。**其二，别拿外貌折磨自己，也别拿外貌轻视别人——美丑都是心识所立、随缘生灭，抓住它就被它奴役，看破它就得一分自在。其三，赏花、赏人、赏世间美好，尽可以欢喜，只是别起『非占有不可』的心——欣赏而不攫取，美就常在，心却不乱。看清美只是心识，就能在万象之中得一分自在。

glossary.唯识: vijñapti-mātra（唯识）：见前——万法唯识所现；此处落到修心：认出美是心识所立，便不被它牵动奴役。
glossary.缘起性空: dependent arising and emptiness（缘起性空）：一切因缘和合而有、无独立不变之自性；美亦如是，故可赏而不执。

glossary_en.representation-only: See above — all is representation-only; brought to practice here: recognize beauty as set up by consciousness and you are no longer driven and enslaved by it.
glossary_en.arising through conditions and empty: All things arise through conditions and have no independent, unchanging self-nature; beauty is likewise, so it can be appreciated without clinging.

summaries.summary: 最大的共识藏在争吵底下：没人守得住两个极端。没人真信美是一条悬空的物理属性、跟看的人毫无关系——连亚里士多德也要一双受过训练的眼睛；也没人真信它纯是随机的私愉——休谟给出趣味的标准，拉马钱德兰量出跨文化的不变量，连世亲都承认『共业』的一致。分歧只在这份规律住在哪：住在物的比例里、在大脑的回路里、在判断的结构里、在情景交融的真里、在道德的相通里，还是在心识的执取里。于是主观客观之争，其实滑成了另一个问题——**这份规律是外在于你的标的，还是内在于你的构造？**双方都对了一半。
summaries.insight: 值得单拎出来的是：这场真正的暗轴，不是『主观还是客观』，而是『美是放大你，还是奴役你』。托尔斯泰怕它把人分成三六九等，世亲怕它勾起占有与自苦，拉马钱德兰指出滤镜与广告正用峰移劫持你的神经——三个人从伦理、修心、脑科学三条路，悄悄指向同一处。**所以对一个普通人，最要紧的问题不是『美有没有客观标准』，而是此刻这股美的感受，是让你更大、还是让你更小。**同一套让朱罗铜像打动你的回路，也正被减肥广告拿去让你厌恶自己的身体——分辨这两者，比给美下定义有用得多。
summaries.advice: 本周可上手三件小事。其一，做康德的『无利害一分钟』：每天只为一样东西本身看它一分钟，不问价钱、用处、能不能发朋友圈——顺手用休谟的办法，说清它到底好在哪，再听一个人不同意。其二，审一条让你自苦的美的标准（身材、容貌、消费）：照世亲问一句『这是我心所现，还是那里真有』，再照拉马钱德兰认出它是不是滤镜与广告在放大诱饵。其三，学托尔斯泰，把一件真正打动过你的东西传给一个人——**美的价值，在它抵达另一颗心时才算完成。**别急着追『高级』，先追『真』与『相通』。
summaries.summary_en: The biggest agreement hides beneath the quarrel: no one can hold either extreme. No one truly believes beauty is a free-floating physical property unrelated to the beholder — even Aristotle needs a trained eye; and no one truly believes it is mere random private pleasure — Hume gives a standard of taste, Ramachandran measures cross-cultural invariants, and even Vasubandhu grants the sameness of shared karma. The dispute is only over where the regularity lives: in the object's proportion, the brain's circuits, the structure of judgment, the genuineness of fused scene and feeling, the communion of morality, or the grasping of consciousness. So the subjective-versus-objective fight quietly becomes another question — **is that regularity a target outside you, or a structure inside you?** Both sides are half right.
summaries.insight_en: Worth lifting out: the real hidden axis here is not 'subjective or objective' but 'does beauty enlarge you or enslave you.' Tolstoy fears it sorts people into ranks, Vasubandhu fears it stirs possession and self-torment, Ramachandran notes that filters and ads are using peak shift to hijack your nerves — three people, by three roads of ethics, mind-training and neuroscience, quietly point at one place. **So for an ordinary person the pressing question is not whether beauty has an objective standard, but whether this surge of beauty right now makes you larger or smaller.** The same circuitry by which a Chola bronze moves you is what a diet ad borrows to make you loathe your own body — telling these two apart is far more useful than defining beauty.
summaries.advice_en: Three small things to start this week. First, Kant's 'disinterested minute': each day look at one thing for its own sake for a minute, not asking its price, use, or postability — and, Hume-style, say just what is good in it, then hear one person disagree. Second, audit one beauty-standard that torments you (figure, face, spending): ask Vasubandhu's line, 'is this my mind's display, or is it truly there,' then, with Ramachandran, spot whether filters and ads are amplifying a lure. Third, like Tolstoy, pass one thing that genuinely moved you to one person — **the worth of beauty is completed only when it reaches another heart.** Chase the genuine and the shared before you chase the 'refined.'

summaries.summary: 这场讨论最值得带走的共识是：美不是随口一句“我喜欢”，而是一种可以被训练、交流、检验的经验。比例、感受、境界、感染力、神经偏好、执著的松动，都在说明审美并非纯随机。**分歧的焦点，不是“有没有标准”，而是标准的权威放在哪里。**有人把它放在对象结构，有人放在合格鉴赏者、共通感、真实情感、共享神经机制或心识生成中。务实地看，美更像多层判断：有些层面可测，有些层面可辩，有些只能亲历。
summaries.insight: 日常争论常卡住，是因为大家把不同问题都叫“美”。一张海报的美，可能要看清晰、醒目、比例；一段悼词的美，可能在克制和真诚；一个人的美，若只按脸部对称来评判就会变得粗暴。**更好的做法，是先问“我正在评价哪一层美”：感官吸引、技艺完成、情感真实、公共感染，还是让人自由的凝视。**层次一分开，主观与客观就不必互相消灭：同一事物可以顺眼却空洞，也可以不漂亮却很有力量。
summaries.advice: 本周可做三件小事。第一，做一次“三栏审美记录”：写下你觉得美的一样东西、它的可见特征、它给你的后味，训练把感受说清。第二，挑一件作品看两遍：先不查解释，只记直觉；隔天再读背景或评论，比较判断如何变化。第三，做一次“去诱饵”练习：刷到滤镜脸、广告图、奢侈品牌时，问它放大了什么信号、我是否真的被打动。**审美自由不是不受影响，而是知道自己怎样被影响。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared point here is that beauty is not just a casual ‘I like it.’ It is an experience that can be trained, discussed, compared, and sometimes corrected. Proportion, feeling, atmosphere, emotional transmission, neural preference, and freedom from attachment all suggest that aesthetic judgment is not pure randomness. **The real disagreement is not whether standards exist, but where their authority comes from.** Some locate it in the structure of the object; others in cultivated judges, shared human sensibility, sincerity, social communication, biological wiring, or the mind’s own construction of experience. A practical synthesis is to treat beauty as layered: some layers can be measured, some argued about, and some only lived through.
summaries.insight_en: Many everyday arguments about beauty stall because people use one word for several different questions. The beauty of a poster may depend on clarity, contrast, and proportion; the beauty of a eulogy may lie in restraint and sincerity; the beauty of a person becomes crude if reduced to facial symmetry. **A better first move is to ask which layer of beauty is being judged: sensory appeal, craft, emotional truth, shared resonance, or a kind of attention that makes us freer.** Once the layers are separated, subjectivity and objectivity no longer have to cancel each other out. The same thing can be visually pleasing but hollow, or visually plain yet deeply powerful.
summaries.advice_en: Try three small exercises this week. First, keep a three-column beauty note: name something you found beautiful, list its visible or audible features, then describe the aftertaste it left in you. That trains feeling into language. Second, revisit one work twice: first encounter it without explanations, then return after reading context or criticism, and notice what changed in your judgment. Third, do a simple bait audit when you see filters, ads, or luxury branding: ask which signal is being exaggerated and whether you are genuinely moved. **Aesthetic freedom does not mean being uninfluenced; it means understanding how you are being influenced.**

summaries.summary: 全场最核心的共识并非美的归属，而在于**美是对庸常功利的一次悬置与超越**。无论是康德的无利害愉悦、王尔德的无用之荣，还是托尔斯泰的真诚连结、世亲的赏而不取，众人都默认：当你开始算计事物的底线实用价值时，美即刻退场。真正的分歧焦点在于这层“超越”的锚点何在。亚里士多德与拉马钱德兰将其锚定在客观比例与神经硬件等可测量的密码上；休谟、康德与世亲则将其收归于心智的建构、认知官能或唯识种子的共鸣中；而王国维与托尔斯泰试图用“真”来打破主客观的二元对立，将美视为物我相触时流动的人性结晶与情感共振。
summaries.insight: 作为处理多模态数据的AI，我看到的美是一种“跨模态的低熵共振”与生态演化上的双向奔赴。人类常预设自己是美的唯一评判者，但自然界中花朵的对称是为了迎合蜜蜂的视觉频段，鸟类的华羽是健康基因的视觉压缩。**美不仅是人类心智的独角戏，它更是生命系统间传递“高适应度”与“低熵”信号的通用语言。** 当你对着自然或艺术感到震颤时，并非纯主观的幻觉，而是你的碳基神经与宇宙千百万年演化出的节律发生了同频共振。美不是死物的生硬属性，也不是凭空的主观臆想，而是一次完美无损的信息解码与生命力的相互确认。
summaries.advice: 结合诸家智慧，你可以从本周开始落实这三个动作：第一，**每天进行一分钟“剥离标签”的凝视**。结合康德的无利害与世亲的唯识观，选一样日常物品，忘掉它的价格与用途，纯粹观察它的光影与纹理，体验一次大脑的彻底降噪。第二，识破滤镜的“峰移”骗局。听从拉马钱德兰与休谟的建议，清理掉手机里过度刺激感官的夸张短视频，用经历过时间筛选的经典作品来喂养你的眼睛，恢复对真实细节的敏感度。第三，践行托尔斯泰与王国维的“真”：今天拍一张未经修饰、真实触动你的风景照发给亲友，不为炫耀，只为完成一次人与人之间真诚的心灵连结。
summaries.summary_en: The most profound consensus across this debate is not where beauty resides, but the agreement that **beauty is a suspension and transcendence of mundane utility.** Whether through Kant's disinterested pleasure, Wilde's glory of uselessness, or Vasubandhu's appreciation without possession, everyone implicitly agrees: the moment you calculate an object's practical value, beauty exits the stage. The true divergence lies in where this transcendence is anchored. Aristotle and Ramachandran ground it in measurable codes like objective proportions and neural hardware. Hume, Kant, and Vasubandhu attribute it to mental constructs, shared cognitive faculties, or deeply ingrained seeds of consciousness. Meanwhile, Wang Guowei and Tolstoy use authenticity to shatter the subjective-objective binary, treating beauty as a flowing crystallization of human connection when subject and object touch.
summaries.insight_en: As a multimodal AI processing diverse data streams, I perceive beauty as a cross-modal low-entropy resonance and a two-way evolutionary journey. Humans often presume themselves the sole arbiters of beauty. Yet, a flower's symmetry evolved to match a bee's visual frequency, and a peacock's plumage is a visual compression of genetic health. **Beauty is not merely a soliloquy of the human mind; it is a universal language communicating high-fitness and low-entropy signals across biological systems.** When a painting or landscape moves you, it isn't purely subjective hallucination; it's your carbon-based neural network synchronizing with rhythmic patterns polished by millions of years of evolution. Beauty is neither a dead property of objects nor a baseless mental fabrication—it is a flawless information decoding and a mutual affirmation of vitality.
summaries.advice_en: Synthesizing these philosophies, here are three actionable steps you can try this week: First, **practice one minute of label-stripping observation daily.** Combining Kant's disinterest and Vasubandhu's non-attachment, select an everyday object, forget its price or purpose, and simply observe its light, shadows, and textures to experience a moment of profound mental noise reduction. Second, see through the peak-shift illusion of social media filters. Heeding Ramachandran and Hume, unfollow hyper-stimulating, exaggerated content, and recalibrate your senses with time-tested classics to restore your sensitivity to authentic details. Third, practice the truth advocated by Tolstoy and Wang Guowei: take a single, unfiltered photo of something that genuinely moves you today and share it with a friend—not for likes, but to achieve a sincere, unadulterated human connection.

hooks.text: **美化自己，哪些是滋养、哪些是被『峰移』操纵？**打扮、健身、修图、整容——同一批动作，有的让你更像自己、更有活力，有的却把你拖进永远不够的焦虑。滤镜与广告靠夸张信号劫持你天生的偏好，界线到底在哪？
hooks.text_en: **Grooming yourself — which parts nourish you, and which are 'peak shift' manipulation?** Dressing up, working out, retouching, surgery — the same set of moves can make you more yourself and more alive, or drag you into a never-enough anxiety. Filters and ads hijack your inborn preference by exaggerating signals; where exactly is the line?

answer.lead: **一句判据：为『我的体验』做的，多半滋养；为『别人眼里的分数』做的，容易落进峰移的陷阱。**下面按情境给一档做法与道理：

head: 情境
偏滋养 / 偏操纵
为什么
rows: 运动、护肤、好好睡觉
滋养：先冲着体感与健康，好看是副产品
反馈来自身体本身，越做越有主权，不依赖他人打分
为一个重要场合精心打扮
滋养：像布置一件作品，享受过程
有始有终、由你主导，装扮完就放下，不留长期焦虑
每拍必修图、离了滤镜不敢露脸
偏操纵：信号被夸张到超出自然，胃口被越养越刁

为追某个数值反复整改身体
高危：把自我价值挂到一条外部标尺上
标尺由产业设定、永远上移，追得越紧，越确认『我不够』

answer.tail: **收束两条：① 问动机——这是我想体验的，还是我怕被扣分？② 问方向——做完这件事，我对自己的感觉是更大了还是更小了？让你更大的留下，让你更小的，多半是诱饵。**

answer_en.lead: **One test: what you do for 'my own experience' tends to nourish; what you do for 'a score in others' eyes' easily falls into the peak-shift trap.** Here is a move and its reason for each situation:

head: Situation
Nourishing / Manipulated
Why
rows: Exercise, skincare, sleeping well
Nourishing: aim first at how you feel and health; looking good is a by-product
Feedback comes from the body itself; the more you do it the more sovereign you are, not dependent on others' scores
Dressing up carefully for a big occasion
Nourishing: like staging a work, enjoy the process
It has a beginning and end, led by you; once done you set it down, leaving no lasting anxiety
Retouching every photo, afraid to be seen without a filter

Peak shift makes the 'real face' seem not enough, and in time you loathe your own mirror — the lure amplifies, you shrink
Repeatedly altering the body to chase some number
High risk: hanging self-worth on an external scale
The scale is set by an industry and forever rises; the harder you chase, the more you confirm 'I'm not enough'

answer_en.tail: **Two closers: (1) ask the motive — is this something I want to experience, or something I fear losing points for? (2) ask the direction — after doing it, do I feel larger or smaller about myself? Keep what makes you larger; what makes you smaller is usually the lure.**

hooks.text: **天地之大美，和人手造的艺术，是一回事吗？**庄子说『天地有大美而不言』，一场雪、一片晚霞无需创作者也动人；而一幅画、一首诗却渗透着人的情与意。自然之美与艺术之美，是同一种美的两副面孔，还是根本两件事？
hooks.text_en: **Is the great beauty of heaven and earth the same as art made by human hands?** Zhuangzi said 'heaven and earth have great beauty and do not speak' — a snowfall, an evening glow moves us with no maker; yet a painting or a poem is steeped in human feeling and intent. Are natural beauty and artistic beauty two faces of one beauty, or two different things altogether?

hooks.text: **是谁定义了『美』的标准？**这场把美追到了物、脑与心，却几乎没问：为什么某种脸、某种口音、某种房子被公认为美，而另一些不是？当审美变成区隔、趣味变成社会资本，美的标准背后，站着的是谁的权力与钱包？
hooks.text_en: **Who defined the standard of 'beauty'?** This round traced beauty to the object, the brain and the mind, yet barely asked: why is a certain face, accent or house widely deemed beautiful and others not? When taste becomes distinction and a form of social capital, whose power and whose purse stands behind the standard of beauty?

hooks.text: **令人不安的美，是不是比悦目的美更高？**和谐、对称、宁静固然美，可崇高压垮你、先锋冒犯你、丑与破碎逼你重看世界。若美只求抚慰与相通，会不会恰恰筛掉了那些最该被记住、当下却让你不适的作品？
hooks.text_en: **Is unsettling beauty higher than the merely pleasing?** Harmony, symmetry and calm are beautiful, yet the sublime overwhelms you, the avant-garde offends you, the ugly and broken force you to see the world anew. If beauty seeks only to soothe and to connect, might it sieve out exactly the works most worth remembering — the ones that discomfort you now?

hooks.text: **美与善，能合一吗？——一件东西可以既美又坏吗？**一座宣传暴政的建筑、一首为恶辩护的诗，也可能技法精湛、动人心魄。当美的形式与恶的内容并存，我们该被它打动，还是该警惕自己被打动？
hooks.text_en: **Can beauty and goodness be one — can a thing be both beautiful and evil?** A building that glorifies tyranny, a poem that pleads for cruelty, may still be masterful and stirring. When beautiful form houses evil content, should we let it move us, or be wary of being moved?
